title: Basic-open sections detect quasi-isomorphisms after open-subscheme restriction
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $g\in A$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=D(g)$, and $i:F\to J$ a morphism of integer-indexed complexes of module sheaves [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $R$ be restriction to the localized site over $U$ followed by the canonical equivalence with $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then the $A$-linear map of section complexes $\operatorname{affineOpenSections}(A,U)(i)$ of [def-sc-principal-open-alternating-total] is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if $\Gamma(U,Ri)$ is a quasi-isomorphism over $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, using global sections of [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Neither complex is assumed quasi-coherent, K-injective, or bounded.

source.place: Tag 08D2, A-linear sections on principal opens; Tag 08BS for the open-subspace restriction convention. Explicit restriction-of-scalars identification for the definitions used here.

proof.text: Put U=D(g). The overFunctor restricts the sheaf to the localized open site. The overEquiv functor identifies that site with the opens of the open subscheme. Global sections of the resulting module identify naturally with the original module sections on U, with their O(U)-action. Applying the ring map A to O(U), obtained from GammaSpecIso followed by restriction, gives exactly the A-action in modulesSpecToSheaf and affineOpenSections. Naturality identifies the induced section maps, and degreewise compatibility with differentials identifies the complexes.

Restriction of scalars is exact and reflects isomorphisms: kernels, images and quotients have unchanged underlying additive groups. Its homology comparison is therefore invertible, and a homology map is invertible precisely when its scalar restriction is. Apply this in every integer degree, and transport across the natural identification from step 1. This gives both directions for any i. If U is empty, section modules are zero, so the same argument still applies.
